parsedVerdict.reasoning: MaintenanceService is a domain-layer (business) file. Its calls to VehicleTable and WorkOrderTable are allowed: business may depend on persistence, and those tables are injected through the constructor, so this is dependency wiring rather than misplaced I/O. There are no framework decorators, base classes or ORM types. The business rules (hours estimate limits, one open order per vehicle, vehicle service state, overrun) belong in the domain. However, every error the service throws carries an HTTP status code: 400 for a bad estimate, 409 for a duplicate open order, and 404 for an unknown vehicle or work order. Choosing transport status codes is a delivery-layer concern. Embedding them in thrown domain errors means the domain is throwing HTTP errors, which the rubric names as a failure for domain files. FleetError itself is a project-declared business type, so the problem is the HTTP status values, not the class. Confidence is moderate because the codes are plain numbers in the file rather than types imported from a web package or the delivery layer.

violations.message: Domain service throws errors carrying HTTP status codes: FleetError(..., 400) and FleetError(..., 409) in open(), and FleetError(..., 404) in the private vehicle() and order() helpers. Mapping failures to HTTP statuses belongs to the presentation/delivery layer (e.g. WorkshopController), not the business domain.
